title: Renewal & expansion checkin - Lakeside Bancorp
next_steps: Send updated pricing for Dedicated 2-pool option
Share SOC 2 and network architecture docs (VPC/KMS)
Schedule benchmark run in us-east-1 with customer's sample workload for next week
Draft contract amendment to add eu-west-1 region and updated commit term
action_items: Maya: send pricing and region SKU breakdown by 2026-08-02
Raj: schedule benchmark and request example workload by 2026-08-04
David Park: provide sample traffic profile & peak concurrency by 2026-08-03
Sarah Liu: confirm procurement timeline & legal reviewers by 2026-08-06
topics: Capacity upgrade: Dedicated GPU pools and autoscaling
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on upgrading Dedicated capacity, adding eu-west-1 region, and aligning procurement timeline. Customer asked for pricing options, SOC 2 + network docs, and a benchmark run with their workload. Action items assigned and follow-ups scheduled.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, we'll run about 45 minutes, quick agenda — renewal status, capacity needs, region add, and next steps.
00:12 Sarah Liu: Sounds good. Morning from our side, we're just trying to sync with procurement and infra.
00:20 Raj Patel: Hi all, Raj from Redwood infra team. We'll be focused on the benchmarks and the dedicated sizing recommendations.
00:28 Peter Gomez: Hey, Peter here. Wanted to call out our peak windows — end of month batch jobs and daytime spike for fraud detection.
00:42 Maya Thompson: Great, that's helpful. Quick refresh, your current Dedicated pool is a 4-GPU commit in us-east-1 on our Standard profile, correct?
00:51 David Park: Yep, that's right, 4 GPUs. Latency's fine for most flows but token cost and throttle during spikes are our pain.
01:05 Maya Thompson: Understood. For renewal you're looking at a 12-month commit, and you expressed interest in adding eu-west-1 for regulatory/residency reasons?
01:16 Sarah Liu: Correct, eu-west-1 is a must for about 30% of our traffic and some customers require EU data residency.
01:27 Raj Patel: Ok, from a technical perspective adding eu-west-1 is straightforward, we can provision a second Dedicated pool there, same model versions. The tradeoff is capacity doubling unless you use routing/fallback policies to share loads.
01:45 Aisha Rahman: Question — can we have VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for the eu region?
01:52 Lena Ortiz: Yep, we support customer KMS and private networking for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can do VPC endpoints and KMS integration, though there are some network config steps.
02:08 Sarah Liu: And audit logs? We need immutable logs for a compliance audit next quarter.
02:12 Raj Patel: We have per-request audit logs and access trails; they can be exported to your SIEM or S3 with retention policies. Small caveat, exports for longer retention are an add-on.
02:30 Peter Gomez: Cost — what's the incremental cost to spin up eu-west-1 Dedicated?
02:35 Maya Thompson: We'll send a SKU breakdown, but ballpark is about 30-35% higher per GPU in eu-west-1 due to cloud infra and capacity premiums. You can also use routing to only route EU traffic to eu-west and failover to us-east under constraints.
02:55 David Park: If we keep a smaller commit in eu-west and rely on failover, what does throttling look like?
03:02 Raj Patel: Throttling behavior follows the pool's reserved capacity; with smaller commit plus autoscale you'll see longer queue times during global spikes. We recommend a warm standby and prefix caching to reduce cold-starts.
03:20 Maya Thompson: For your renewal, we outlined two main options — upgrade to a single bigger commit in us-east and cross-region on-demand, or a two-pool dedicated commit (us-east + eu-west). We're proposing a Dedicated 2-pool option as discussed.
03:35 Sarah Liu: Procurement wants clear SLAs for latency and uptime. Do you have SLA numbers per region?
03:41 Maya Thompson: Yes, we have 99.9% uptime for Dedicated with latency targets based on model family; we'll include per-route latency percentiles in the SLA addendum.
03:58 Peter Gomez: Benchmarks — we want to run our e2e workload, can you run perf with our sample traffic?
04:05 Raj Patel: Absolutely. Please share a 24-hour sample with peak concurrency and request size distribution; we'll run a benchmark in us-east and eu-west. Preferably we run the bench during a low-usage window to minimize noise.
04:22 Sarah Liu: We'll get that to you. Timeline — procurement is aiming EOM for a signed amendment if numbers look ok.
04:30 Maya Thompson: Good to know. On pricing structure, would you consider a 12-month commit with a 20% uplift for region add vs a 24-month with deeper discounts?
04:40 Markus Veazey: From procurement, we'd prefer 12-month, but open to 24 if discounting is meaningful. Need finance to run numbers.
04:52 Raj Patel: Quick technical note — quantization profiles we're recommending for your workload (2:1 speed-up on generation) may change latency slightly; we'll include quality/regression evals as part of the bench.
05:08 Aisha Rahman: Are model versions pinned across pools? We can't have different model outputs in different regions.
05:14 Raj Patel: You can pin model versions in deployment config; we also support automatic rollouts with canary and A/B but you can pin to exact checksum to ensure consistency.
05:30 Peter Gomez: Security — SSO and RBAC, we need SCIM for provisioning and roles mapped to our AD groups.
05:37 Lena Ortiz: SCIM and SAML are supported; we can map RBAC roles to groups and enforce MFA via your IDP.
05:44 David Park: Network latency concerns for cache warming across regions — is there shared KV cache?
05:50 Raj Patel: We don't share KV cache across regions for isolation; we do prefix caching per-region. For cross-region warm starts you can pre-warm keys or use traffic routing to bring warm sessions. There's some replication options for private deployments but they add complexity.
06:10 Sarah Liu: Ok. Also curious about burst capacity — on busy days we might have short bursts 5-10x baseline, can you handle that?
06:18 Maya Thompson: We offer burst capacity add-ons and autoscaling policies; for Dedicated we can configure a burst pool or short-term overcommit depending on headroom. We'll outline the recommended autoscale policy in the doc.
06:35 Peter Gomez: Any vendor lock concerns if we move more to Dedicated?
06:38 Maya Thompson: No lock, you manage model versions and data. Dedicated just reserves infra; you can export models and logs.
06:46 Sarah Liu: Competitors — we've also been looking at AWS Bedrock and Anthropic for some routes, what's your angle?
06:53 Maya Thompson: Our focus is predictable inference economics and multi-environment parity — same API and ops across hosted/dedicated/private, plus observability like token-level cost breakdowns, which help with unit economics.
07:08 Markus Veazey: Legal will need a region addendum and updated indemnities; can you provide a draft?
07:15 Maya Thompson: Yes, we'll have legal draft the amendment for eu-west-1 and updated terms.
07:22 Peter Gomez: On contract length — if we do 24 months and bigger commit, do you offer pricing caps?
07:28 Maya Thompson: We can include a pricing cap clause for committed units; we'll propose a tiered discount schedule in the proposal.
07:36 Raj Patel: For the bench, what's your SLO for p95 latency we should aim to validate?
07:42 Sarah Liu: Aim for p95 under 350ms for short chat flows and under 1.2s for longer multi-turn generations.
07:50 Raj Patel: Got it. We'll target those and report percentiles plus token costs.
08:00 Aisha Rahman: Any hidden costs we should be aware of? Eg export charges, long-term log retention?
08:06 Lena Ortiz: Exports to S3 and long-term retention are billed separately; we'll itemize those in the pricing sheet.
08:15 David Park: For the benchmark, do you simulate KV cache behavior? Our workloads are cache-sensitive.
08:20 Raj Patel: We'll run with prefix/KV cache enabled and also a cold run to show delta. We'll capture token-level costs for both.
08:32 Sarah Liu: Ok that's helpful. So next steps recap?
08:36 Maya Thompson: Recap: Maya will send updated pricing and region SKU breakdown; Raj will schedule and run benchmarks once Lakeside shares workload; we'll include SOC 2, network/KMS docs; legal will get a draft amendment for eu-west-1.
08:50 Markus Veazey: Timeline — purchase order targeted for next month, pending bench results and legal review.
09:00 Maya Thompson: Sounds good. Any other blockers?
09:03 Peter Gomez: None from engineering. We'll send the sample traffic by end of week.
09:08 Sarah Liu: Procurement will try to expedite.
09:12 Maya Thompson: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pricing doc and schedule for the benchmark.
09:18 (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript includes some auto-caption errors — e.g., K-V cash instead of KV cache in one section, 'V-P-C' heard in a few places. The team decided on Dedicated 2-pool recommendation and benchmarks to validate p95 latency and token cost. Actual action items recorded above.
